code: library(mfrmr) calibration_responses <- read.csv(   "calibration-responses.csv", colClasses = "character", na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) gpcm_fit <- fit_mfrm(   calibration_responses,   person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"), score = "Score",   model = "GPCM", method = "MML",   step_facet = "Rater", slope_facet = "Criterion",   rating_min = 0, rating_max = 2, category_policy = "preserve",   mml_integration = "adaptive", quad_points = 31,   maxit = 400, reltol = 1e-10 ) summary(gpcm_fit, profile = "fit", detail = "brief") draft <- extract_mfrm_calibration(   gpcm_fit, calibration_id = "rubric-calibration",   source_fit_id = "training-cohort", scoring_quad_points = 141 ) review_mfrm_calibration(draft) calibration <- freeze_mfrm_calibration(validate_mfrm_calibration(draft)) save_mfrm_calibration(calibration, "gpcm-calibration.rds") library(mfrmr) # A later session needs only this file and the new response rows. calibration <- load_mfrm_calibration("gpcm-calibration.rds") new_responses <- read.csv(   "new-responses.csv", colClasses = "character", na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) scores <- score_mfrm_calibration(   calibration, new_responses, missing_response = "omit" ) score_review <- summary(scores) score_review score_review$review score_review$settings$score_integration_review plot(scores, type = "interval", preset = "publication", top_n = Inf)  # Keep full-precision scores and every Person's disposition, including those # without scores. The complete object supports later review and plotting. write.csv(scores$estimates, "person-scores.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "") write.csv(scores$person_dispositions, "person-review.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "") saveRDS(scores, "scored-cohort.rds") retained <- scores$settings$retained_prior_identity  # Sensitivity analysis on the same calibration scale, not a new population fit. alternative <- score_mfrm_calibration(   calibration, new_responses, missing_response = "omit",   scoring_prior = list(mean = retained$mean + 0.5, sd = retained$sd * 1.25) ) summary(alternative) library(mfrmr)  calibration <- load_mfrm_calibration("reviewed-calibration.rds") new_rows <- read.csv(   "new-responses.csv",   colClasses = "character",   na.strings = "",   check.names = FALSE,   fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM" ) scores <- score_mfrm_calibration(calibration, new_rows) print(scores) plot(scores, type = "interval", preset = "publication") write.csv(scores$estimates, "person-scores.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Constraint settings: noncenter facet = Person; anchored levels #> = 0 (facets: none); group anchors = 0 (facets: none); dummy facets = none. Centered facets #> sum to zero across all levels, including anchors and group totals. #>  #> Results. #>  #> Scale functioning. #> Category counts were available for all 4 categories: 0 unused and 0 below 10. Counts alone #> do not establish category adequacy. Adjacent threshold comparisons: 0 decreasing among 2 #> available; 0 of 2 comparisons unavailable. Available estimates range from -1.22 to 1.06 #> logits. Adjacent threshold comparisons: 0 decreasing among 2 available; 0 of 2 comparisons #> unavailable. #>  #> Facet measures. #> Person measures ranged from -1.72 to 1.51 logits (M = -0.16, SD = 0.82). Rater measures #> ranged from -0.61 to 0.41 logits (M = 0.00, SD = 0.40). Criterion measures ranged from #> -0.34 to 0.22 logits (M = 0.00, SD = 0.30). #>  #> Fit and precision. #> Overall mean-square fit was within the 0.5-1.5 screening band (infit MnSq = 0.87, outfit #> MnSq = 0.86). This band is the package's review convention; published mean-square #> guidelines differ, and band position is screening evidence rather than a model-validity #> decision. MnSq outside [0.5, 1.5]: 18 of 57 classified elements flagged; 0 of 57 elements #> unclassified. Largest misfit signals among 57 elements with complete paired statistics: #> Person:P022 (|ZSTD| = 2.88); Person:P026 (|ZSTD| = 2.84); Criterion:Content (|ZSTD| = #> 2.27). Criterion reliability = 0.87 (separation = 2.56). Person reliability = 0.66 #> (separation = 1.41). Rater reliability = 0.68 (separation = 1.45). Separation reliability #> describes differences among facet locations relative to their estimation errors. High #> Person values indicate distinguishable abilities; high rater values indicate #> distinguishable severities, not inter-rater agreement. Low rater values can also reflect #> imprecision and do not establish agreement. The index does not test every rater pair or #> quantify the practical size of severity differences. Reliability, separation and Strata are #> approximate compatibility indices using marginal SEs; joint-information SEs do not validate #> this variance decomposition. They do not account for covariance among estimates. EAP-based #> separation is not posterior-variance EAP reliability. Model and fit-adjusted values are #> companion indices, not confidence limits. Strata describes hypothetical distinguishable #> strata, not discovered groups. Facet heterogeneity chi-square summaries use diagonal SE #> weights, not full-covariance joint tests. The Person row uses EAP measures with posterior #> SDs, which yields a conservative summary that is not numerically comparable to JMLE-based #> person reliability from FACETS. Inter-rater agreement for Rater is reported separately from #> separation reliability. Diagnostics match scores within Person and all remaining non-rater #> facets; each compared pair contributes one opportunity per matched context. The denominator #> is 138 matched-context opportunities across rater pairs, not a count of independent people. #> 6 of 15 candidate rater pairs have matched scores. Observed exact agreement = 0.39; #> observed adjacent agreement (absolute score difference at most 1, including exact matches) #> = 0.86; model-expected exact agreement = 0.35. The model-expected baseline uses fitted #> category probabilities with calibration fixed; it is not chance agreement or an inferential #> test. It assumes conditional independence at the saved Person point score (EAP for MML), #> rather than integrating over the Person posterior. These descriptive summaries do not #> classify rater quality or establish fairness. Element-level 95% approximate intervals #> (Normal approximation) accompany 57 of 57 estimates; 57 of 57 estimates have intervals #> eligible for primary reporting. #>  #> Residual structure. #> Overall categories: 0 flagged among 4 classified; 0 of 4 unavailable. Step/scale groups: 0 #> flagged among 1 classified; 0 of 1 unavailable. Facet levels: 1 flagged among 9 classified; #> 0 of 9 unavailable. Level pairs: 1 flagged among 9 classified; 0 of 9 unavailable. Expected #> counts condition on the same responses through Person posteriors, with fitted calibration #> held fixed. Residual scales omit cross-response covariance and calibration-parameter #> uncertainty; thresholds are descriptive, not calibrated tests. Strict marginal screening #> gives an overall RMSD of 0.01, overall max |standardized residual| = 0.43. The largest #> strict marginal cell involved Criterion: Content | Cat 4 (standardized residual = -1.53, #> proportion difference = -0.06). Strict pairwise local-dependence follow-up flagged 1 level #> pair(s) under the latent-integrated agreement screen. The largest strict pairwise signal #> involved Rater: R04 vs R05 (exact-agreement standardized residual = 2.09, #> adjacent-agreement standardized residual = 0.22). #>  #> Reporting cautions. #> Fit-basis note: MnSq/ZSTD fit statistics in this run were computed at EAP person measures, #> which are shrunken toward the population mean; they are therefore not numerically #> interchangeable with JMLE-based engines such as FACETS. Refit with method = "JML" when a #> JMLE-style residual basis is required for external comparison.

code: normal_rule <- function(n) {   jacobi <- matrix(0, n, n)   jacobi[cbind(1:(n - 1), 2:n)] <- sqrt(1:(n - 1))   e <- eigen(jacobi + t(jacobi), symmetric = TRUE)   list(nodes = e$values, weights = e$vectors[1, ]^2) }  pattern_mass <- function(fit, membership, patterns, order) {   rule <- normal_rule(order)   theta <- fit$calibration$person_sd * rule$nodes   gamma <- sqrt(fit$calibration$variance) * rule$nodes   answer <- numeric(nrow(patterns))   for (h in seq_along(theta)) {     logw <- outer(theta[h] + gamma, 0:2) -       matrix(c(0, cumsum(fit$calibration$steps)), order, 3, byrow = TRUE)     prob <- exp(logw - apply(logw, 1, max))     prob <- prob / rowSums(prob)     conditional <- rep(1, nrow(patterns))     for (block in split(seq_along(membership), membership)) {       block_prob <- matrix(1, order, nrow(patterns))       for (j in block) {         block_prob <- block_prob * prob[, patterns[, j] + 1L, drop = FALSE]       }       conditional <- conditional * as.vector(crossprod(rule$weights, block_prob))     }     answer <- answer + rule$weights[h] * conditional   }   answer }  evaluate_parallel_plan <- function(fit, membership) {   stopifnot(inherits(fit, "mfrm_testlet"),     length(fit$input$columns$facets) == 0L,     identical(as.numeric(fit$input$score_levels), 0:2 + 0),     length(membership) == 4L, !anyNA(membership))   patterns <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:2), 4)))   data <- data.frame(Person = rep(sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81), each = 4),     Task = rep(membership, 81), Score = as.vector(t(patterns)))   scores <- predict(fit, data, quad_points = 61)   stopifnot(identical(scores$table$Person, sprintf("Y%02d", 1:81)),             all(scores$table$Status == "available_conditional"))   low <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 61)   probability <- pattern_mass(fit, membership, patterns, 121)   tab <- scores$table   v <- fit$calibration$person_variance   expected_variance <- sum(probability * tab$ConditionalSD^2)   stopifnot(abs(sum(probability) - 1) < 1e-8,     max(abs(low - probability)) < 1e-8,     abs(sum(probability * tab$Estimate)) < 1e-7,     abs(sum(probability * (tab$ConditionalSD^2 + tab$Estimate^2)) - v) < 1e-7)   list(scores = scores, probability = probability, patterns = patterns,     membership = membership, summary = data.frame(       RMSPosteriorSD = sqrt(expected_variance),       ModelImpliedEAPReliability = 1 - code: toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")  fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",   method = "JML", model = "RSM", maxit = 300 ) diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none") dif <- analyze_dff(fit, diag, facet = "Rater", group = "Group", data = toy) rpt <- dif_report(dif) cat(rpt$narrative) #> Mean observed-minus-expected scores were compared for the Rater facet across levels of Group. 4 of 4 group comparisons had sufficient observations to report a residual difference. Differences are in score units. They do not isolate differential functioning: group residual means can differ even when response parameters are the same. No p-values, confidence intervals or positive/negative classifications are provided.

code: ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core") fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",   model = "RSM", method = "MML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,   category_policy = "preserve") intervals <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", method = "sandwich") summary(intervals) #>   Target   Estimate         SE       Lower       Upper    ModelSE  ModelLower #> 1    R01 -0.1838153 0.08409258 -0.34863371 -0.01899684 0.08209147 -0.34471159 #> 2    R02 -0.3088478 0.07488878 -0.45562708 -0.16206847 0.08298771 -0.47150069 #> 3    R03  0.1795027 0.08434452  0.01419045  0.34481490 0.08202273  0.01874108 #> 4    R04  0.3131604 0.09478720  0.12738087  0.49893987 0.08294736  0.15058652 #>    ModelUpper    Status CIEligible #> 1 -0.02291895 available       TRUE #> 2 -0.14619486 available       TRUE #> 3  0.34026428 available       TRUE #> 4  0.47573421 available       TRUE #>                                                                                                            InferenceReview #> 1 Pointwise normal approximation under the selected covariance method; numerical availability does not guarantee coverage. #> 2 Pointwise normal approximation under the selected covariance method; numerical availability does not guarantee coverage. #> 3 Pointwise normal approximation under the selected covariance method; numerical availability does not guarantee coverage. #> 4 Pointwise normal approximation under the selected covariance method; numerical availability does not guarantee coverage. plot(intervals)   # Compare two selected raters, rather than each rater against the origin. # Here choose the first two example labels; prespecify your own comparison. raters <- unique(as.character(ratings$Rater)) contrast <- matrix(0, 1, length(raters), dimnames = list(   paste(raters[1], "minus", raters[2]), raters)) contrast[1, 1:2] <- c(1, -1) difference <- mfrm_facet_intervals(fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast) summary(difference)[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Lower", "Upper", "Status")] #>          Target  Estimate        SE      Lower     Upper    Status #> 1 R01 minus R02 0.1250325 0.1337755 -0.1371626 0.3872276 available # With the default negative rater sign, a positive contrast means the first # rater is stricter. Units are native logits. An interval containing zero # leaves the direction uncertain; it does not establish equivalence.  # Estimate the population SD in this same model before standardizing. # Even an intercept-only population model needs one row per person. persons <- unique(ratings["Person"]) population_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"),   "Score", model = "RSM", method = "MML", population_formula = ~ 1,   person_data = persons, person_id = "Person",   rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve", quad_points = 61) standardized <- mfrm_facet_intervals(population_fit, "Rater",   contrasts = contrast, scale = "standardized") #> Warning: Population-SD-standardized contrasts use full joint delta-method uncertainty; sampling coverage is not qualified. Regular inference requires a correctly specified, identified marginal model and a true population SD strictly above zero. A positive fitted SD alone does not establish these conditions; near-zero SD can make the ratio unstable. Quadrature agreement is a numerical diagnostic, not an error bound. Unequal slopes or steps can make expected-rating differences vary with ability. summary(standardized) #>          Target  Estimate       SE      Lower     Upper  ModelSE ModelLower #> 1 R01 minus R02 0.1284989 0.138447 -0.1428523 0.3998501 0.138447 -0.1428523 #>   ModelUpper    Status CIEligible #> 1  0.3998501 available       TRUE #>                                                                                                                 InferenceReview #> 1 Population-SD-standardized pointwise delta-method interval; source numerical checks passed, sampling coverage is unqualified. #>                                   ScaleReference NativeEstimate #> 1 within-facet zero-sum contrast / population SD      0.1244346 #>   CoverageQualified #> 1             FALSE #>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            InferenceCaution #> 1 Population-SD-standardized contrasts use full joint delta-method uncertainty; sampling coverage is not qualified. Regular inference requires a correctly specified, identified marginal model and a true population SD strictly above zero. A positive fitted SD alone does not establish these conditions; near-zero SD can make the ratio unstable. Quadrature agreement is a numerical diagnostic, not an error bound. Unequal slopes or steps can make expected-rating differences vary with ability. # Estimate is now in fitted ability-population SD units; its delta-method # interval includes uncertainty in that SD. It is not a Wald z statistic.  # CML estimates the native contrast without an ability distribution. if (requireNamespace("lpSolve", quietly = TRUE)) {   cml_fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",     model = "RSM", method = "CML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,     category_policy = "preserve")   cml_ci <- mfrm_facet_intervals(cml_fit, "Rater", contrasts = contrast)   summary(cml_ci)   apa_table(cml_ci)   file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # Choose a lasting path for your analysis   saveRDS(cml_ci, file)   saved <- readRDS(file)   summary(saved) # Same conditional-information result, without refitting   # Use plot(saved) for a figure; ordinary mfrm_results() does not accept CML. } #>          Target Estimate        SE      Lower     Upper    Status CIEligible #> 1 R01 minus R02 0.124638 0.1335936 -0.1372007 0.3864767 available       TRUE #>                                                                                                             InferenceReview #> 1 Pointwise conditional-information normal approximation; numerical availability does not guarantee finite-sample coverage. #>     ModelSE ModelLower ModelUpper #> 1 0.1335936 -0.1372007  0.3864767

title: Display saved GPCM intervals and bootstrap results — plot.mfrm_slope_intervals
text: Crosses retain unavailable intervals. Open circles retain intervals infinite endpoints; plot replace finite bounds. Incomplete intervals retain computed endpoint tick, without connecting interval line. missing endpoint infinite endpoint calibrated one-sided interval. Finite review-bounds use dashed line. table retains IntervalStatus, CIEligible, CIUse (saved), bounds failure reasons; returned notes explain display. bootstrap LRT, histogram shows resolved null statistics line observed statistic. returned notes count every unresolved replicate. Use apa_table() target-aware tables, plot_data() plotted values, as_ggplot() customization. Attach one result named list mfrm_results(fit, intervals = list(slopes = ci, curves = curves), compute = "never"). Named plot routes become gpcm_slopes, gpcm_curves, etc. Exact source matching required; default fit diagnostics preserved. export_mfrm_results() saves tables plots; replay reloads saved RDS, preserving selected methods without rerunning estimation. Markdown report summaries include finite, unbounded unavailable interval counts saved inference cautions/reasons. positive slope ratio intervals spanning many orders magnitude, use as_ggplot(ci) + ggplot2::scale_x_log10(). Finite bounds estimates must strictly positive. Keep linear axis signed differences. Changing axis narrow interval make reliable.

High Person values indicate distinguishable abilities; high rater values indicate distinguishable severities, not inter-rater agreement. Low rater values can also reflect imprecision and do not establish agreement. The index does not test every rater pair or quantify the practical size of severity differences. Reliability, separation and Strata are approximate compatibility indices using marginal SEs; joint-information SEs do not validate this variance decomposition. They do not account for covariance among estimates. EAP-based separation is not posterior-variance EAP reliability. Model and fit-adjusted values are companion indices, not confidence limits. Strata describes hypothetical distinguishable strata, not discovered groups. Facet heterogeneity chi-square summaries use diagonal SE weights, not full-covariance joint tests. Ordinary JML uses exploratory location precision; these indices are screening summaries, not structural confidence intervals.

frequentist coverage not exact #>  Exact normal-model interval for positive mean-square expectation #>           MLS approximation; pointwise coverage is not guaranteed #> G/Phi are dimensionless; SEM is in score units. Available describes calculation, not coverage. #> For differences, positive G/Phi and negative SEM favor the comparison plan. #> Method assumptions and limitations: $notes; complete saved results: $intervals. # One row per plan for absolute dependability; the complete table is retained. subset(s$table, Metric == "Phi",   select = c(Tasks, Estimate, Lower, Upper, Status)) #>   Tasks  Estimate     Lower     Upper    Status #> 3     6 0.6205514 0.1453685 0.8782785 Available #> 4    12 0.7658521 0.2538371 0.9351952 Available # Reuse an interval for a curve, with no interval calculation. p <- plot(d, metric = "Phi", intervals = s$intervals$Phi, draw = FALSE) plot_data(p, "notes") #>           Type #> 1     subtitle #> 2      caption #> 3  uncertainty #> 4  uncertainty #> 5  uncertainty #> 6  uncertainty #> 7  uncertainty #> 8  uncertainty #> 9  uncertainty #> 10 uncertainty #> 11 uncertainty #>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Text #> 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Future complete crossed designs | Saved coefficient intervals | Source-study uncertainty #> 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Points are requested scenarios; lines are guides.  #> 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Nominal 95% intervals; method: Generalized CI under normal effects. #> 4                           Ribbons connect saved endpoints at requested counts; intermediate plans are not evaluated. Isolated intervals use vertical segments. Open points have no interval; gaps are not interpolated. Inspect unavailable_intervals and the saved interval objects for reasons and diagnostics. #> 5                                               Ribbons do not establish simultaneous coverage across scores or metrics. Any joint coverage across plans depends on the interval method and its stated model; drawing a band adds no coverage guarantee. Interval overlap does not test a score or plan difference. #> 6                                                                                                                                                                    Phi includes the random facet main effect in absolute error. Independent normal effects and a complete balanced one-facet source are required. #> 7                                                                                                                                           This generalized confidence interval does not guarantee exact frequentist coverage. More pivotal draws reduce numerical error, not model uncertainty or coverage error. #> 8                                                                                                                           The GCI truncates its pivotal numerator at zero, not the source variance estimates. PointStatus and Status describe separate outputs; a zero endpoint is not proof of zero uncertainty. #> 9                                                                                                                              The monte_carlo attribute contains separate 95% numerical bands for the endpoints. Increase draws if these bands affect the intended decision; save the whole result with saveRDS(). #> 10                                                                                                          All future counts transform the same single-rating interval and use source degrees of freedom. Rows are dependent; overlap does not test a plan difference. These are not pass/fail accuracy intervals. #> 11 Widths lost to floating-point resolution leave endpoints and their numerical bands unavailable. A base pivotal interval with lost resolution cannot supply difference bounds, including for identical plans. Diagnostic single-rating bounds remain in pivot; the sampled zero atom retains its separate status.

Prior: Standard #>   normal N(0,1). #>   95% intervals: continuous posterior quantiles. #>   Posterior SDs and intervals condition on point estimates of the calibration #>   and prior; their estimation uncertainty is excluded. #>  #> Empirical draw summaries (first 10) #>  Person Draws MeanValue SDValue LowerValue UpperValue #>   NEW01     3    -0.373   0.323      -0.56          0 #>   Draw limits are empirical quantiles at the requested level. These deterministic design summaries do not establish arbitrary-facet simulation support or parameter-recovery performance. #>  - The structural design review reports deterministic bookkeeping and conservative design guidance, not DIF/bias detection power.
